info.title: id — X.TLD application integration contract
info.description:
The application-handoff protocol of the `id` identity service for first-party applications under the configured PARENT_DOMAIN (written `X.TLD` throughout; `localsplash.ai` URLs anywhere are deployment examples only, never normative).

This is id's own protocol, NOT standard OIDC. There is no application secret and no webhook HMAC in the POC contract: browser authorization is public, and every server-only endpoint is trusted by TLS plus an explicit IPv4/CIDR network policy.

## Network trust (server-only endpoints)

`POST /api/token`, `POST /api/apps/register`, `GET /api/events`, and all `/api/directory/*` endpoints accept a request only when the caller's resolved IPv4 peer is inside the `ID_TRUSTED_APP_CIDRS` allowlist (comma-separated IPv4 CIDRs; `/32` and bare addresses supported). The TCP socket peer is authoritative; `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured only when the direct peer is inside `ID_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, and then only across trusted hops evaluated right-to-left. Malformed, IPv6, IPv4-mapped-IPv6, and non-allowlisted addresses are rejected deterministically with a generic 403. This authenticates a trusted server/network, not an individual application: applications sharing an allowed egress IP can call the same endpoints — accepted for the first-party POC on a controlled host, and NOT suitable for unrelated or customer-hosted X.TLD applications.

## Flow

1. `GET /authorize?redirect_uri&state` (public, browser). `redirect_uri` must be HTTPS on X.TLD or a subdomain.
2. id redirects back with a one-time `code` (and the echoed `state`).
3. The application's CIDR-trusted server redeems it at `POST /api/token` with the exact `redirect_uri`.
4. The same server registers at `POST /api/apps/register` and catches up from `GET /api/events?since`.

## superAdmin provenance (pinned)

`user.superAdmin` in the token response is session-scoped and never stored on `id_tbl_User`. For an existing SSO session, `/authorize` copies `id_tbl_Session.bSuperAdmin` into `id_tbl_AuthCode`; redemption returns the consumed code's `bSuperAdmin`. For a fresh provider login, id calculates the value once and writes the same value to both Session and AuthCode. Redemption NEVER recalculates privilege from the email.

## Event delivery (outbound id → application)

id POSTs events to the registered `webhook_url`. The receiving application's endpoint allowlists id's egress IPv4/CIDRs; TLS protects the transport. Deliveries carry `X-Id-Event`, `X-Id-Event-Id`, and `X-Id-Timestamp` headers; event ids and timestamps are what idempotency/replay handling keys on (the same event id can arrive more than once). An `X-Id-Signature` HMAC header MAY be present for legacy receivers and is OPTIONAL to verify — it is not part of the POC contract.

servers.description: X.TLD is the configured PARENT_DOMAIN (placeholder, normative).

get.description: With a live SSO session, immediately 302s to `redirect_uri` with a one-time `code` (and echoed `state`). Otherwise shows the login page and completes the redirect after authentication. Codes are single-use, expire in 5 minutes, and are bound to the exact `redirect_uri` they were minted for.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: HTTPS URL whose host is X.TLD or any subdomain of it. Nothing else is accepted.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value echoed back verbatim on the redirect.

post.summary: Redeem a one-time handoff code (CIDR-trusted server only)
post.description: The `redirect_uri` must exactly match the one the code was minted for (exact redirect binding). Codes are single-use and expire 5 minutes after minting; a replayed, expired, or re-bound code yields 400. No client secret is required by the POC contract — admission is the IPv4/CIDR policy. `user.superAdmin` is the consumed code's `bSuperAdmin` (see superAdmin provenance); it is never recalculated from the email at redemption.

400.description: Missing fields, or an invalid, expired, reused, or re-bound code.

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

post.summary: Register the application's event endpoint (CIDR-trusted server only)
post.description: Called by every app on boot; idempotent per origin. `webhook_url` must be HTTPS on X.TLD or a subdomain. id immediately queues a `ping` delivery to prove the endpoint is reachable.

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

get.description: Events after `since`, oldest first. Combined with idempotent handling of pushed deliveries (dedupe on event id), this closes any gap from downtime without polling.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Last event id already processed; defaults to 0.

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

post.summary: Idempotently ensure a central user by email (CIDR-trusted server only)
post.description: Creates the user if no user holds the normalised email, otherwise returns the existing one; concurrency-safe, and a repeated `idempotencyKey` returns the UID the first call produced. A pre-created user is `claimed: false` until a trusted-provider login with a matching verified email attaches an identity — untrusted providers can never claim a UID by asserted email. No client-secret header or body field is accepted on any directory endpoint, in any deployment mode.

200.description: The ensured user (minimal fields only — never identities, sessions, codes, or OAuth credentials).

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Literal substring matched against email and displayName.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: the `nextCursor` of the previous page; 0 for the first page.

400.description: limit or cursor out of bounds.

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

get.summary: Fetch one central user by iUserId (CIDR-trusted server only)

403.description: Caller's resolved IPv4 peer is not allowlisted.

code.description: The one-time handoff code from the /authorize redirect.

redirect_uri.description: Must exactly match the redirect_uri the code was minted for.

superAdmin.description: Session-scoped. Provenance: existing SSO Session → AuthCode → redemption; a fresh login writes the same calculated value to both Session and AuthCode. Redemption never recalculates from email.

identity.description: The login method this particular sign-in used.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS URL on X.TLD or a subdomain where the app receives events.

secret.description: Legacy webhook-HMAC secret. OPTIONAL to use: POC receivers trust network policy (allowlist id's egress IPv4/CIDRs) plus TLS and are not required to verify signatures.

signature.description: Describes the legacy, optional signature scheme.

id.description: Strictly increasing; the idempotency/replay key. The same id can be delivered more than once — handlers must dedupe on it.

claimed.description: True once any login method is attached — a trusted-provider login with a matching verified email claims a pre-created UID; untrusted providers never can.

DirectoryUser.description: Deliberately minimal: never identities, sessions, codes, or OAuth credentials.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when this is the last page.

error.description: Generic; 403 bodies never disclose the policy or the resolved peer.

correlationId.description: Present on 403s; matches the server log line carrying the resolved peer IP.
